utterances.text: And so you didn't -- that would be roughly 180 days, and you saw him five or six times out of those 180 days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I saw him more times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, I thought you just said that -- I thought you just testified on direct that you saw him five or six times inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I saw him outside the camp. Within the Building Number 6 I saw him five or six times and outside I saw him more times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. You saw him five or six times inside Hangar 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So it was an unusual occurrence for Mr. Delic to enter Hangar 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand. It was the interpreter. Was it "really" or "rarely"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Your Honour, if I can have just a second while I go through my notes, I believe I'm about done. You talked about the water supply on direct. You said you got some water in bottles, not as much as you wanted and sometimes you didn't get it for many days. Were there -- do you recall whether somebody would ever hose you all down inside Hangar 6, just bring in a hose and ... did that ever occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Who have you discussed your testimony with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where? The question is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us start off with here in The Hague. Did you discuss your testimony with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the name. I've forgotten it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Is it that smiling gentleman over there with the moustache?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have forgotten the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: My learned friend. Okay. Is he the only person in The Hague that you have discussed your testimony with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Before you came to The Hague who did you discuss your testimony with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you remember: were they representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor or were they defence lawyers or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Which? Defence lawyers or officers --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Representatives of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And that was after you gave your statement on February 21st 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One more time they came after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And did you sign another statement while they were there that second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't sign any statement. They just read out the statement I had given the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And those are the -- by the way, did you have a chance to correct that statement either time you talked to the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And when you talked to the Prosecutor before you testified here, did he show you your statement again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Did you look at any other papers in preparation for your testimony here today, any other documents or pictures or videotapes or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Besides discussing your testimony with the Prosecutor here and your testimony with the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor before you came here, have you talked about your testimony with anybody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: One last question and one last series of questions. I think we are done then. At any time while you were in Hangar 6 were there ever beds provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't get beds. We got some kind of benches towards the end of my stay there in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Were there mattresses on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I pass the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Greaves, you may proceed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, I have got just two matters that I want to discuss with you this afternoon, please. You have given evidence to this Tribunal today that on one occasion when you were in the camp you went to an office and spoke to Mr. Mucic, and Hazim Delic was present, and you were interrogated about the question of sleeping with Bosnian girls. Do you remember giving us that evidence earlier on today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You clearly remember this incident of speaking with Mr. Mucic, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You have already told their Honours this afternoon that you recall being interviewed by and making a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in February of last year; that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. Moran, who has just been asking you questions, went through that process with you, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what you told the court was that what you put in your statement was the truth to the best of your knowledge and recollection; that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I could remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, please refer to the statements, which I think you have got beside you if you need to refresh your memory, but would you like to tell the court, please, why it was that in that statement that you made to the Office of the Prosecutor you made no mention whatever of that conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would you like to explain to the court why in the statement that you made to the Office of the Prosecutor, which you say was the truth to the best of your knowledge and belief, why did you not mention this conversation in that statement, Mr. Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, that being so, Mr. Kuljanin, would you like now to tell the court, please, why it was in that statement you said this: "I never spoke with Mucic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which sentence is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Let me just draw your attention to it. Do you have the Serbo-Croat version? I am sure that will be easier for you to look at, Mr. Kuljanin. I do not want to be unfair to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would your Honour just give me a moment, please? . I am struggling with the Serbo-Croat version. Have you got the Serbo-Croat copy there, Mr. Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Could you look, please -- I think it is going to be the fourth page, please. I would like you to count down until you get down to a paragraph which begins: "Pavo Mucic ..." Do you see that one? I just want you to read it to yourself, please, for the moment so you can refresh your memory. Do not tell us what is in it. Just read it, please. Have you read that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And it says there, does it not, Mr. Kuljanin now that you have refreshed your memory, "I never spoke with Mucic"; does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but when I was giving this statement I was always hurrying to go to work, so I was not able to always give complete information all the time, so every time when I was giving information I was in a hurry to get to work, so I did not have enough time to think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What I suggest to you, Mr. Kuljanin, is this: it is not in the statement, that conversation, and you said you had never spoken with Mr. Mucic, because that conversation simply never took place, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did, but I forgot to put it in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So what you are saying now is it is not true effectively when you say: "I never spoke to Mr. Mucic." Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true that I did speak to Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So what you put in your statement, that is a complete fabrication, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Asked and answered. He gave an answer to this contradiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I suspect the point is well made. I shall move on. I want to ask you now one final question, Mr. Kuljanin. When you speak of Mr. Mucic wearing uniform, you saw him wearing green military style clothing. That is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage, camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Camouflage, but he had no insignia of any kind, no badges, no rank or anything like that, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe he did. I do not recall. I did not dare look. I was ordered -- under orders to look down, not sideways.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So you cannot say whether or not he had any insignia of any kind, can you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see. I'm not in a position to say. I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kuljanin. I have no further questions for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other questions? Any other defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Mr. Kuljanin, good day, good afternoon. I am Edina Residovic, and I defend Mr. Zejnil Delalic. I'm glad to meet you. Mr. Kuljanin, I will make a request before I move on to the questions that I will ask of you just to clarify one matter. When your introduction was announced yesterday, your appearance, since before you another witness by the name of Kuljanin was at the stand, we are from the same region, so please could you tell us whether in the Konjic and Jablanica areas in Northern Herzegovina there are families with a large number of members with the same name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Such families like Kuljanin, Zuza, Zivak, Cecez, Azinovic, Dzumhur, Delalic do exist among all ethnic groups in that region; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We clarified this matter before this Trial Chamber; a number of witnesses bearing the same name will appear. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, before this Trial Chamber you gave a statement under oath; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you still want to speak the full truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Kuljanin, is it correct that you lived permanently in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that one year before these combat operations that you refer to you became a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, let me ask this question in a more precise manner. You were a member of the SDS; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall. I really don't remember. It was a long time ago in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then I will make a little digression. You answered to my learned colleague, Mr. Moran, that you did not recall certain things; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that your lack of memory is a result of everything that you went through in this period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, consequences of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then it is true that on some events you can talk on the basis of something else than your memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I am talking about it from my memory and what I don't remember I will not talk about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But when you make different statements in different statements that you give that is because of your lack of memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecutor you stated that you mostly helped your family in the agricultural work, farming; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do not recall being a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I may have been but I don't recall really.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember that you had no function in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I had no function in the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did know Rajko Dordic, your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you remember in that period of time of April and May you did some work, office work, in the office of Rajko Dordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not true. I don't even know of an office of Rajko Dordic. He was a captain of the JNA and he worked in Konjic. I was never in his office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this information. Do you know that Rajko Dordic came to his birthplace in May and remained there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Rajko Dordic organised the defence of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no defence of Bradina. It did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, I would like to go back to your previous testimony. You stated that you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in February 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned colleague posed a question to you, you said that you also spoke to the representatives of the Prosecutor when you arrived in The Hague and read the statement that was given to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please could you confirm for me that when my learned colleague, Mr. Greaves, asked you a question you said that you gave the statements always in a hurry, that you could not reflect well, because you were in a hurry to go to work every time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, every time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Kuljanin, is it true that you gave multiple statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, please answer whether every time you gave statements you gave it in a hurry because you went to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in a hurry. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please if you look at your -- page 1 of your statement in Serbo-Croatian language, the date stated there was February 21 1996; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That means that you were there only one -- you went there only on one day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is different from the answer to the question by the esteemed colleague, Mr. Greaves, that every time you went to give a statement you did it in a hurry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A statement was -- I gave the statement on one occasion and the second time when it was read back to me, and the first time was when it was -- when I had given it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying this point for me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you also testified that you personally did not have any position in any military formation in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where in Bradina is the Albanija hamlet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this hamlet is at the very entrance of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were seen in Albanija on the barricades that were erected there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Albanija is in the middle of Bradina, not in the beginning or the end of it. That's where I lived. That's where my house was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So now we know the location of this hamlet Albanija. Could you then answer the question that you have been seen several times on the barricades in Albanija, which you helped erect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no barricade there and I did not help put it up, and no one in my village did it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, do you know Drasko Koprivica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Drasko Koprivica was wounded in the course of these combat operations in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not wounded during the operations. He was wounded when he tried to escape, when he tried to move to the other territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, is it true that he surrendered together with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because we tried to escape, and Drasko was then wounded and then we returned to the village and he went home and I stayed with my father, with my mother and my sister. That was in the morning of 26th at 6 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, it was Rajko Dordic who asked you to return to the village with Rajko Koprivica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, together with the group of Rajko Dordic you tried to escape from Bradina to the Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you said nothing about this fact during your questioning in February of 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, now you do remember that at the request of Rajko Dordic you returned to Bradina together with Drasko Koprivica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to Bradina but to my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your village where on 27th, as you stated, you surrendered to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, your brother, Milenko, continued with this group, which was moving towards the territory under control of the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother was not in the group with me. When I was returning to Bradina I met my brother, who was part of the group that was trying to break through towards the Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, there were several barricades erected ramps in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that since you have problems with your memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, many problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you do not recall certain facts. Do you remember that immediately before these combat operations and the war you were seen -- you were frequently seen in a uniform of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who? Me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you lived in Konjic, that is in Bradina, you know that in Bosnia-Herzegovina a state of immediate war threat was declared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't, because the last month before this we did not have any electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If there is -- if the immediate war threat was -- had been proclaimed, you would have known?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not listen to the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any event it is true that you did not join the Territorial Defence or the reserve police in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody had asked me to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you were not aware of the official call by the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you explained how you were brought to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to confirm that when you were climbing onto the truck, as you stated, you were severely beaten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was twice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also other people who were transferred -- transported in this truck were also severely beaten; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your truck no women or children were loaded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. They were separated in front of the Mico's cafe.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Celebici, as you testified, you recognised Mario Matic, who was your school friend in Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mario Matic is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a uniform on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you also stated that in Celebici after your arrival there you gave a statement to the members of a commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what commission it was. It wasn't a commission. Two investigators.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: One of them you recognised as Miroslav Stenek; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This commission behaved correctly towards you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, so-so, not bad and not well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No force was applied to you in the period of this hour while you were in interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I had to say everything that they wanted me to do. I had to say "yes" even though things were not that way. I had to say "yes".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will come to that question, but there was no physical force applied to you during this interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were sitting in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were standing in front of this commission. Thank you. You just told me that you had to state that everything they were asking of you was true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Everything they wanted. They could, you understand. I had to say the way they wanted, not the way I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, because you had to, as you are testifying before this court, you said that you were issued two pieces of weapon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They asked you about weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I had to say that I had weapons because I knew what was coming.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you said that -- so you confirmed that you had weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not confirm. I said that I did have them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They did not suggest it to you beforehand. They just asked you whether you had arms, weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that you had weapons, or when they asked you if you had weapons, what was your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said "yes".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say on that occasion that the automatic rifle you received from Stevan Gligorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you state then on the second occasion you received a semi-automatic rifle from Dragan Vujicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think, Ms Residovic, we will break here for tomorrow morning. You can continue your cross-examination then. Now before we close today, I think the motion which we have for tomorrow, because of some other reasons, we are shifting it to Wednesday, the 14th of this month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are motions that I mentioned at the beginning of the session today that we would ask that the court take up prior to the next two prosecution witnesses. I am wondering if the court has had an opportunity to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We are examining our schedule and seeing how we can bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You have made your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: So we will examine it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
